messages.subject: Whether there’s an option to increase the sensitivity of ENMO for Verisense created using GGIR?
parts:
I am comparing Actiwatch data with Verisense.  Whether there’s an option to increase the sensitivity of it so that the peaks of the data match with  Actiwatch?

Also, there seems a delay between ActiWatch and Verisense. Whether there are some data points missing for Verisense, or of there’s a sync issue between both sets of data.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Whether there’s an option to increase the sensitivity of ENMO for Verisense created using GGIR?
parts: I am comparing Actiwatch data with Verisense.  Whether there’s an option to increase the sensitivity of it so that the peaks of the data match with  Actiwatch?

GGIR offers the choice between a number of acceleration metrics and connected parameters, some may be more similar to what Actiwatch does with its data than others. I do not know which metric/parameter combination is best to imitate Actiwatch data. I believe there is literature on this. I am happy to investigate this for you as a paid consultancy.
Also, there seems a delay between ActiWatch and Verisense. Whether there are some data points missing for Verisense, or of there’s a sync issue between both sets of data.

GGIR intentionally starts at an integer number of large epochs (default length is 15 minutes) relative to the hour to ease interpretation and comparison of results across individuals. So, if your recording was started at 8:54 then you will see output from 9:00 onward. This means that when you compare with Actiwatch data always align the data based on timestamps. Needless to say that I do not know how time is handled in Actiwatch software, so it is always good to double check synchronisation visually at multiple time points in the recordings.

Best,
Vincent
